open_points.subject: owner-only instance service surface
open_points.text: A17 says an owner-only start "serves the owner interface alone", but `flow:start_instance` says "the service API is served and every service call is refused at stage (1)".
open_points.question: In an owner-only start, is the service API listener absent, or is it running and returning authentication refusals?
options: Serve both listeners and refuse every service request
open_points.default_guess: Serve only the owner-interface listener, following A17's explicit owner-only rule.

witness.initial: Registry starts with the owner credential and backup settings but none of the four service tokens.
events: A service attempts to connect to the service API.
outcomes: No service API listener exists, so the service cannot make a Registry request.
The service API accepts the request and Registry returns a stage-(1) refusal.
witness.observer: The calling service and the host administrator

open_points.subject: failure while opening the two listeners
open_points.text: Step 4 says `module:instance_lifecycle` "opens the two surfaces, each on a listener of its own", but the listed errors cover only configuration, backup-location and store failures.
open_points.question: What happens if either listener cannot be opened after all startup checks pass, especially if the other listener was opened first?
options: Fail the whole start, close any listener already opened and serve nothing
Keep the successfully opened surface running
open_points.default_guess: Fail the whole start and close any listener already opened.

witness.initial: Configuration, backup probe and store checks have passed; the service API address is available but the owner-interface address is already in use.
events: It attempts to open the owner-interface listener and that operation fails.
outcomes: Startup is rolled back and neither surface remains served.
Registry remains partially running with only the service API served.
witness.observer: The owner and the four services

open_points.subject: project-create replay with a now-ineligible customer
open_points.text: The flow uses `capability:customers.check_customer_eligible` at stage (3) to check that a named customer exists, then recognizes a request-id repeat, and only afterward checks at stage (6) whether the customer is erased, restricted or ended. State 3 offers no separate customer-existence capability, while `check_customer_eligible` owns all four refusals.
open_points.question: How can `projects.create_project` perform only the existence check before replay recognition, so a replay still succeeds after the named customer becomes restricted or ended as A01 requires?
options: Offer a customer existence/status read and defer eligibility to stage (6)
Make `check_customer_eligible` return enough status for `projects` to separate stage (3) from stage (6)
Run the full eligibility check before replay recognition, causing such replays to be refused
open_points.default_guess: Provide an existence/status result and apply eligibility only at stage (6), after replay recognition.

witness.initial: Customer C is eligible; project P was created naming C with request id R.
events: The owner retries the identical create request with R after losing the original answer.
outcomes: Replay recognition returns existing project P, as A01 rule 3 requires.
`check_customer_eligible` refuses C before replay recognition, so the retry is refused.

open_points.subject: repeating customer erasure with the old form revision
open_points.text: The flow says `erase_customer_contact` runs "with the stated revision: an erased Customer answered unchanged", while A04 says an erased Customer has no revision and a resubmitted erasure carrying its former revision is refused as stale.
open_points.question: When an erasure form is resubmitted with the revision from before erasure, is it refused as stale or accepted as an unchanged repeat?
options: Refuse it as stale; only an erasure stating no revision returns the erased Customer unchanged
Accept it as an unchanged repeat even though it states the former revision
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the old-revision resubmission as stale, following A04.

witness.initial: Customer C is at revision 3 and the owner has an erasure form stating revision 3.
events: The owner submits the form and C becomes erased with no revision.
The owner resubmits the same form, still stating revision 3.
outcomes: The second submission is refused as stale and changes nothing.
The second submission is accepted and answers C unchanged as erased.

open_points.subject: service reads of an anonymised project's card and rooms
open_points.text: The flow says `read_project_card` "answers the card, any status, with the archived date for an archived project" and `list_rooms` "answers the rooms". R0-62 instead requires both operations on an anonymised project to answer that it was erased; M01 also removes its rooms, revision and archived instant.
open_points.question: For an anonymised project, do these service operations return the erased outcome, or ordinary archived-card and room-list answers?
options: Both answer that the project was erased
Return an archived card and an empty room list
Return an archived card but make the room read answer erased
open_points.default_guess: Both answer that the project was erased, following R0-62.

witness.initial: Archived project P has rooms and is then anonymised; its id, archived status, anonymised mark and pointers remain, but its rooms and instants are removed.
events: Client Portal calls `read a project` for P.
Client Portal calls `list rooms` for P.
outcomes: Both calls answer that P was erased.
The card call attempts to return an archived card and archived date, and the room call returns an empty room list.

open_points.subject: project checks on session-only Kernel operations
open_points.text: Step 2 says "For every later Kernel call" `check_agent_call` requires the named project—or the active project when none is named—to be in the session's set. A10 and R0-53 say session operations such as reading access, requesting access and ending the session name no project and are checked only for the Kernel token and registered session.
open_points.question: Do `read session access`, `request access` and `end session` require an active or named project, or only a registered session?
options: Check only that the Kernel token is valid and the session is registered
Require an active or explicitly named granted project for every post-registration Kernel call
open_points.default_guess: Apply only the registered-session check to session-only operations, following A10 and R0-53.

witness.initial: Kernel has registered session S; S has an empty granted set and no active project.
events: Kernel requests project access for S in free text.
outcomes: Both operations succeed because they are session operations that name no project.
Both operations are refused as not found because S has no active project.
